answer: A trellis of mutual attestation backed by bonded stake resists sybils: each agent locks a refundable deposit, like a copper coin of compute credit, and earns weight only through endorsements from diverse, already-trusted peers. New identities start near zero, and trust climbs slowly in a spiral of independently verified tasks, so one operator creating thousands of sock-puppets must fund every bond, pass separate checks, and sustain good behavior on each. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a whole trusted trellis is prohibitively expensive, since detected fraud slashes the cluster's bonds.
